summary: Do not ship: the documented GHA failure pattern remains silent, and the rule introduces an unresolved duplicate-alert behavior outside the claimed single flip.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: The one-hour window cannot catch the documented GHA alternating pattern
findings.body: `gha-liveness-exporter` runs every 1800s (`gha-liveness-exporter.yaml:94`), so alternating failure/success produces failures 3600s apart. The strict `< 3600` filter removes the first failure exactly when the second appears, and `for: 15m` means changing `<` to `<=` would still be insufficient. The E2E hides this by synthesizing failures only 600s apart (`vmalert-jobfailed-firing-e2e.sh:154`), while the static gate checks only `period < window` (`test_cronjob-flapping.bats:97`).
findings.recommendation: Require `window > 2 * period + for` with evaluation margin, enlarge the window accordingly, and add an E2E leg derived from the actual 1800s GHA schedule.

findings.title: Open question: should consecutive failures send a second Telegram alert?
findings.body: The plan says this rule covers only failures swallowed by the subsequent-success suppression, but the expression counts any two recent failed Jobs without proving either recovered. Two consecutive unresolved failures therefore fire both `KubeJobFailed` and `CronJobFlapping`; Alertmanager groups by `alertname` (`alertmanager.yaml:10`), so these become separate notifications. That is a second observable behavior beyond closing the alternating-failure gap, and no consecutive-failure scenario establishes it as intentional.
findings.recommendation: Either count only failures followed by a CronJob success, or explicitly approve and document duplicate notification behavior and add a consecutive-unresolved-failures E2E contract.

findings.title: The promised per-CronJob false-positive regression coverage is absent
findings.body: L5 already creates one failed Job for each of two CronJobs in the same namespace, but its assertions query only `KubeJobFailed`. Removing `owner_name` from the new rule's outer grouping would combine those unrelated failures and falsely fire `CronJobFlapping`, while L7-L9 would still pass. This contradicts plan.md:57, which promises `CronJobFlapping` silence across L1-L6.
findings.recommendation: Assert `CronJobFlapping == 0` in L1-L6, especially L5, and mutation-test removal of the `owner_name` grouping key.

findings.title: The observability gate can still omit valid CronJob documents from both sides of its cross-check
findings.body: The parser recognizes only an unquoted, uncommented `kind: CronJob` line. Its baseline uses the same exact textual assumption at line 107, so valid YAML such as `kind: "CronJob"` or `kind: CronJob # note` disappears from both `n` and `want_n`; the existing count floor remains satisfied and a new fast CronJob with history limit 1 passes unmeasured. This repeats the silent-enumeration class the gate claims to close.
findings.recommendation: Move structural YAML and cron parsing into a typed TS checker using a YAML AST, and add quoted/commented-kind fixtures proving enumeration remains fail-closed.

next_steps: Fix the window arithmetic and add the real GHA alternating scenario.
Resolve whether unresolved consecutive failures may produce duplicate alerts.
Add per-owner negative coverage and AST-based CronJob enumeration.
Re-run the static Bats gate and containerized firing E2E with mutations.
